::: {#exm-two-level-normal}
#### A two-level Gaussian model

Observations $Y_{ij}$ come from groups $j = 1, \ldots, J$,
and each group has its own mean $\theta_j$.
A two-level model specifies

$$
\ba
Y_{ij} \mid \theta_j &\sim \ndist{\theta_j,\, \sigma^2}
&& \text{(data given group means)}\\
\theta_j \mid \mu, \tau &\sim \ndist{\mu,\, \tau^2}
&& \text{(group means given hyperparameters)}.
\ea
$$

The group means $\theta_j$ are the group-level parameters,
and $\mu$ and $\tau$ are the [hyperparameters](#def-hyperparameter).
To fit this model by Bayesian inference,
we add a [hyperprior](#def-hyperprior) for $(\mu, \tau)$
and a prior for the within-group standard deviation $\sigma$.
:::
